What comes up in Gosford

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table describes how these jobs generally go in this area. Your block may not match it, which is the reason for looking at it first.

Commercial interior near the centre

Central Gosford stock is older commercial as much as residential, and the material is usually in the services rather than the walls.

How it is handled
Whole building surveyed before the scope is written, then removal sequenced around whatever has to stay open.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists to a control plan, independent assessor for clearance.

Wet area linings in older housing

Bathroom, laundry and kitchen sheeting in pre 1990 Gosford housing, frequently behind newer tiling and cabinetry.

How it is handled
Area isolated and sealed, material removed intact where possible, and the substrate checked because tile adhesive is often asbestos as well.
What does it
Licensed removalists working in a contained area.

Internal strip outs and partial removal

Walls, floors, linings and fit out taken out of a building that stays standing, usually ahead of a renovation rather than a rebuild.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials cleared first, then the removal done by hand so that what remains is not disturbed. Structural elements are identified before anything is cut.
What does it
Hand tools and small plant only, with material carried out and loaded at the kerb.

Gosford

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Pre 1990 stock around the centre Residential and commercial, with the usual assumptions until sampling says otherwise.
  • Apartment redevelopment pressure Which brings larger removals ahead of demolition.
  • Commercial interiors Where material is found in flues, backing boards, floor tiles and adhesives rather than in the obvious places.
  • Occupied buildings Which changes the separation, the monitoring and the hours.

Around central Gosford the working area is often the footprint and nothing more, so material is wrapped, staged and loaded rather than stockpiled. On the residential streets the access is easier and the sequence matters more: seal the area, remove under controls, then independent clearance.

Gosford questions

What people ask before we start

How does asbestos removal fit into a demolition programme?
It comes first. The removal is completed and independently cleared before the structure is touched, which is why the survey sits at the front of the programme rather than somewhere in the middle.
Do you handle commercial asbestos removal?
Yes, as a managed pathway: identification and sampling, licensed removal, air monitoring where it is required, independent clearance and disposal at a licensed facility.
Does sandy ground change how an excavation is done?
Yes. Sandy material drains well and batters poorly, so a face that has to stand is battered back or supported rather than left vertical, and near the water the water table is close enough that dewatering is planned rather than discovered.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
